title: Integer-graded algebras and left module sheaves on a ringed site
statement: Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. On a site $(C,J)$ with a sheaf $R$ of commutative rings, an associative unital integer-graded $R$-algebra $A$ consists of $R$-module sheaves $A^i$, $i\in\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction-compatible $R$-bilinear products $A^i\times A^j\to A^{i+j}$, and a compatible family of identity sections in degree zero, satisfying associativity and the two unit laws. No commutativity of $A$ is imposed. A graded left $A$-module consists of $R$-module sheaves $M^q$, $q\in\mathbf Z$, with restriction-compatible $R$-bilinear actions $A^i\times M^q\to M^{i+q}$ satisfying associativity and the unit law. Morphisms are degree-zero $R$-linear sheaf maps preserving these actions; identities and compositions are degreewise. There is no differential. Evaluation at a degree is the corresponding forgetful functor to $R$-module sheaves. For $U\in C$, restriction to the localized site $C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] restricts each degree and each operation and defines the restriction functor on graded modules.
